answer: Try device fingerprint dedupe. First, the join page draws a hidden canvas and WebGL scene, and tiny GPU and driver quirks yield a hash that differs on nearly every machine. Second, the node adds font and audio-stack timings, then compares each new join against all earlier ones. Third, any match above 90% is folded into the older account and shares its reward. A farm of 500 agents needs 500 machines; used laptops at $150 each run $75,000, and spoofing kits get caught within a week. Calling each copy new is a fable, like one comet over a mesa that every watcher sees as one streak.
